Subject: Session accounting: long-lived contexts and rounding rules

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and KV hit rates looked great. Before we move forward with an evaluation, Procurement has two questions about how Redwood bills our usage so we can model spend across a multi-day pilot:

1) If we keep a session open (same session_id) for >24 hours but traffic is intermittent, how is the context billed? Do you bill by active request tokens only or does the server-side KV/cache retention cause additional context charges?

2) Rounding and minimums: our QA calls are often very short (50–120 tokens). Do you apply a per-request floor, round to a quantum (e.g., 256 tokens), or aggregate over a session window? Any examples would help.

3) Streaming: for long-running streams that push partial tokens (real-time transcripts), are partial fragments rounded at each packet or at final commit?

I attached an anonymized sample usage (sample_usage.csv) showing our expected distribution. Could you share a billing example and any programmatic ways to avoid paying a full quantum for micro-calls? Procurement is also asking whether customized rounding rules can be included in an enterprise contract.

Appreciate it — cc'ing Clare from procurement.

—Samir

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Session accounting: long-lived contexts and rounding rules

Hi Samir — thanks for sending the sample. I've pulled Ben and Marissa in so we can give concrete numbers and a short-term workaround. High level answers first, then a short example: 

- Billing unit: we bill tokens consumed by API calls (prompt + completion) and separately surface a small context-retention charge only for pinned private deployments. For hosted accounts, KV/cache retention itself is not a standalone bill line — you pay only for tokens processed and any committed cache-prefetch credits.

- Session/windowing: Redwood groups requests by session_id into a 6-hour activity window by default for metering aggregation. If there's no activity for 6 hours the session is considered idle and subsequent calls start a new aggregation window. This reduces per-call rounding noise for bursty users.

- Rounding/minimums: default hosted behavior rounds up to the nearest 128-token quantum for each aggregated window per model family. There is a soft floor of 40 tokens per raw API request before aggregation (very short pings).

- Streaming: partial tokens are buffered server-side; rounding is applied at the time the stream is committed (session close or explicit flush). We don't round per packet.

Example (using numbers from your CSV):
- 10 short calls avg 80 tokens each within a 3-hour window => we aggregate and round the sum up to the nearest 128 quantum (total 800 tokens => rounded to 896 tokens billed).
- Long-running session that issues 1 call per day for 5 days (same session_id) with 120 tokens each and >6h idle between calls => each call falls into a separate window and may be rounded separately (5 * 128 quanta billed).

Workarounds:
- Use batched calls where feasible (combine multiple micro-prompts into one request) to reduce rounding loss.
- Explicitly call the flush endpoint to commit streamed tokens together.
- For enterprise customers we can tune the aggregation window and quantum.

Ben/Marissa — can you confirm the numbers and propose a term sheet/discount options if Acme wants customized rounding?

Thanks,

Samir — cc'ing commercial and billing. Short answers then a proposal: 

- Aggregation window: yes, enterprise tenants in Private or Dedicated can request a longer aggregation window (up to 24h) as part of contract configuration. We apply that server-side so there's no SDK change required.

- Floor vs aggregation: the floor applies at the per-request level before aggregation for telemetry/abuse prevention (we don't credit sub-40 pings). However the window-level rounding is applied to the aggregated sum. Practically that means a 20-token ping becomes 40 before being added to the window total.

- Dedicated/reserved: Dedicated customers operate under reserved capacity pricing which supports tighter metering (per-token accounting to the nearest token) when they opt into the "per-token metering" addendum. This is a common clause for committed customers.

Commercial proposal for Acme Pilot: 
- 6-month pilot, committed $85k/month usage => 20% discount on host rates.
- Custom aggregation window: 24h window (server-configured).
- Micro-call protection: exclude any request <40 tokens from floor if monthly committed spend > $200k (we'll add a clause).
- We will produce a sample invoice mapping and include a one-time credit equal to estimated rounding loss for the first month (capped at $3k).

Attached: proposed_pricing_term_sheet.pdf (term sheet with these items). If terms are OK we can put the term sheet into DocuSign and loop legal.

Hi Samir — quick technical/billing note and a worked example so Procurement has a line-item view. 

Metering rules (hosted default unless noted):
- Per-request floor: 40 tokens (applies before aggregation).
- Aggregation window: 6 hours default (server-side). Enterprise config: up to 24 hours.
- Quantum: windows are rounded up to the nearest 128-token quantum per model family.
- Streaming: tokens are committed at stream close/flush; partial packets are buffered and billed on commit.

Worked example (numbers):
Inputs (your sample month):
- 3,200 micro requests (avg 60 tokens each) clustered into 400 windows of activity (avg 8 calls/window).
- 150 long sessions (same session_id) with 1 call per day, 140 tokens each, spaced >6h apart.

Compute (hosted default):
1) Micro cluster aggregate: 3,200 * 60 = 192,000 raw tokens. Floor bumping not material at this scale because most calls >40. Window rounding: 192,000 / 128 = 1500 quanta exactly => billed tokens = 192,000 (no rounding loss).
2) Long sessions: 150 * 140 = 21,000 raw tokens. Because calls are >6h apart they are billed as 150 separate windows => each window rounded to 128 => billed tokens = 150 * 128 = 19,200 (here you actually get a rounding benefit compared to raw tokens).

Net billed tokens = 192,000 + 19,200 = 211,200 tokens.

If you elect the 24h aggregation window (enterprise): the 150 long sessions would aggregate into fewer windows, e.g., if some fall inside a 24h window they'd combine and reduce rounding overhead. Dedicated + per-token metering eliminates quanta rounding altogether.

Next steps: 
- If the commercial proposal from Ben looks good, sign the term sheet and we'll generate a sample invoice that maps your CSV lines to Redwood billing rows (line items: raw tokens, rounding adjustments, credits).
- I can also run a blind invoice simulation this week if you re-send the CSV with timezone markers — that helps estimate how many calls fall into the same 24h window.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to walk Procurement through the sample invoice.
